newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity up in recovery from down trend.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity up in recovery from down trend.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading higher Wednesday in a slight recovery from a down trend earlier this week, industry sources said.
Despite the rising values, little fundamental news was seen influencing the market, the sources said.
"We're moving up slowly, people seem to have more of a feel for the range of the market," said one New York-based futures trader.
As of 1245 EDT, NYMEX July California Oregon Border (COB) was up 29 cents at $17.05 per megawatt hour (MWh) following trades at $17.00-$17.50, while August was up 31 cents at $21.50 per MWh.

July Palo Verde (PV) was trading up 18 cents at $27.00 following exchanges in a range of $26.85-27.40, while August was bid at $29.75 and offered at $30.00 from Tuesday's settlement at $29.74 per MWh.
As of 1205, an estimated 286 PV and 237 COB contracts had traded.
Electricity futures prices eased Monday and Tuesday on mild weather in the U.S. West and rising supplies of power as generation units returned from maintenance and refueling outages.

Parts of the Southwest were experiencing triple digit heat, with an expected high of 103 degrees Fahrenheit in Phoenix, Ariz., on Thursday. But sources said a rise in air-conditioning demand was being offset by generation capacity coming back from spring maintenance outages.
The 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at Palo Verde nuclear station in Arizona returned to 100 percent power early Wednesday. The unit was curtailed Monday to repair a feedwater heater tube leak.
A 150 MW hydro turbine, operated by Seattle City and Light Co, was heard shut for a brief outage.

In the latest six to 10 day forecast, temperatures in the Northwest were called to average near to slightly above normal with above normal temperatures, while readings in the Southwest would run near normal over most of the region but below normal in the far western area.
As of 1245 EDT, July NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down 1.2 cents at $2.11 per million British thermal units.
